generative.title: Between Rules and Chance
generative.subtitle: When rules become a brush, chance leaves a shape
generative.description: Rules, gestures and time together shape the experience of generative art. Begin by finding repetition and difference in the image, then try intervening in the original. Some works leave a result; others continue to change while you stay.
generative.introduction: What happens between code and image? This gallery brings together surfaces left by algorithms, lines shaped by gestures, and continuously computed image and sound. Each work has its own rules, materials and sense of time. Look from a distance, zoom in, wait and interact to find its rhythm. Project % and Ars Electronica documents provide context for FAB DAO's involvement in generative art; they do not mean that every work here belongs to the Hundred Peaks Project.
generative.question: When an artist designs rules, are we looking at a result or at a process?
generative.transition: The next gallery moves from forms built through code toward place. Mountains and islands can be invented terrain, lived memories, or entrances into research and publishing.

islands.title: Mountains Becoming Islands
islands.subtitle: From the outline of a mountain, see islands connected to one another
islands.description: How is a place seen, named and recorded? Move from generative images of mountains and seas to depictions of cities and records of everyday life. Finally, stay at the Nusantara Archive reading table, where landscape opens into relationships between people.
islands.introduction: This gallery treats the island as a question to read slowly. pulau gen builds terrain that does not exist; The Moonlit Sea of Taitung responds to a lived moment of looking; a video of a claw machine in Changhua records an everyday setting. Nusantara Archive is the reading core, exploring exchanges across places through images, interviews, food and translation. These works are not all part of the Hundred Peaks Project. Its public narrative and historical proposals are presented separately as documents showing how connections were once made.
islands.question: If a place is more than a landscape, what other voices, routes and everyday experiences deserve preservation?
islands.transition: Reading connects places with different people's experiences. The next gallery continues the question: when we collect a work, do we also need to care for the relationships it brings?

commons.title: Collecting as a Common Act
commons.subtitle: A work can also be the beginning of a relationship
commons.description: How should a museum collect a work that wants to keep circulating? This gallery begins with a work that encourages changing hands, then moves through gathering, participation, exchange and sharing, read alongside the Art Bank's proposals and institutional documents.
commons.introduction: Collecting may preserve a form, but it may also change what a work set out to do. a collection of collectors encourages editions to keep changing hands, while Your First Green Sofa invites people into discussion. Tickets, commemorative coins and community works leave different forms of participation. Art Bank documents connect these questions with the work of proposing, discussing and selecting. Artists, proposers, holders and museum visitors occupy different positions; the exhibition does not merge them into a 'we' that has already reached consensus.
commons.question: How should a museum collect a work that wants to keep circulating?
commons.transition: The next gallery turns to artistic responses to specific events. Supporting freedom, opposing war, participating in relief and preserving history each require their own context.

memory.title: Silence, Memory, Persistence
memory.subtitle: When voices are hard to preserve, how can collecting respond?
memory.description: A blank sheet of paper can be an entrance, but a shared quiet atmosphere cannot by itself connect different events. This gallery reads the White Paper Movement, the war in Ukraine, earthquake responses, Taiwan's historical images and experiments with words in their own contexts.
memory.introduction: The two entrance works respond to the 2022 White Paper Movement. They are followed by a Ukrainian artist's account of displacement, protest imagery and acts of support. The earthquake video retains the time and place of Turkey and Syria in 2023 before the gallery turns to a fragment of Taiwan's historical images and closes with an experiment in the unmaking of words. This juxtaposition compares how art responds, records or changes meaning; it does not assume a shared trauma or political position. Changes of wall display allow a pause, and each section retains its own sources.
memory.question: When a work leaves a voice, a blank or a fragment, what context must we supply so that memory can continue to be understood?
memory.transition: Return to the museum timeline in the lobby. From early art support, the Hundred Peaks Project and the Art Bank to the 2024 FAB Museum competition, consider how the next exhibition space might care for works.

institution.title: From Supporting Art to Building a Space Together
institution.introduction: FAB DAO's collecting and exhibiting have grown through experiments by artists, community participants and different working groups. This museum begins with verifiable holdings in two Art Bank wallets and selects thirty-two works to read alongside project, proposal and governance documents.
institution.authorship: Works are credited according to the artists' original texts and verifiable sources. The viewing guides originally written in Chinese, the selection and the relationships between works are the museum's editorial interpretations. Artists, proposers, those carrying out acquisitions and visitors occupy different positions; this exhibition's texts do not stand in for historical decisions or the position of the entire community.
institution.collectionScope: The museum's collection data comes from positive-balance snapshots of the Ethereum and Tezos Art Bank wallets dated 2026-09-06. Issuance projects such as Project % are listed separately as project documents. Other funds, treasuries and works transferred out in the past have not yet been comprehensively inventoried.
institution.question: Beyond preserving the shape of works, how can a museum preserve participation, discussion and the possibility of continued change?
